question: What is revenue deficit?

options.text: It is the excess of government's total expenditure over total receipts.
It is the difference between revenue and capital expenditure.
It is the excess of government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
It is the excess of government's capital expenditure over capital receipts.

solution:
The correct answer is, '**It is excess of the government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue** means **income or earnings,** and **deficit** means **shortage.**
 
• A revenue deficit is a condition when expenditure is more than earnings.
 
 
• In some business terms, it means the difference between projected (assumed) income and realized (actual earned) income.
 
 
 
• So,** a revenue deficit is the excess of the government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Excess of the government's total expenditure over total receipts** is called a** fiscal deficit.**
 
• **Capital expenditures** are one-time **long-term expenses**.
 
 
• Examples - ***Machinery, Vehicles, Land, etc.***
 
 
 
• **Revenue expenditures** are short-term and **day-to-day expenses**.
 
 
• Examples - ***Rent, Bills, etc.***
 
 
 
• **Excess of the government's capital expenditure over capital receipts** is a **capital deficit.**
